hints: Focus on what it means for the same oxide to react with both a strong acid and a strong base.
Recall which Period 3 oxide is famously amphoteric and forms an aluminate anion like $[Al(OH)_4]^-$ with NaOH.
Write the outer shell configuration $3s^2 3p^x$ for that element and count just the p electrons to finish.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the oxide type**

An oxide that reacts with both acid and alkali is amphoteric. That is the key clue here.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{amphoteric oxide reacts with acid AND with base}$$

**Identify X in Period 3**

In Period 3, $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{MgO}$ are basic, $\text{SiO}_2$, $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$, $\text{SO}_2$ are acidic. Only aluminium oxide is amphoteric.

Reactions of Y:
$$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 + 6\text{HCl} \rightarrow 2\text{AlCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
$$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 + 2\text{NaOH} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{Na}[\text{Al}(\text{OH})_4]$$
So X is aluminium, Al, where X is part of the anion $[\text{Al}(\text{OH})_4]^-$.

**Count outer shell p electrons**

Aluminium is in Group 13, Period 3. Its full configuration is $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^1$.

Outer shell (n = 3):
$$3s^2 3p^1$$
That is just 1 p electron.

options.A: 0 p electrons would mean an outer shell of $3s^1$ or $3s^2$ only, like Na or Mg. But $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{MgO}$ are basic oxides only, they do not react with NaOH to give an anion containing X.
options.B: X is Al. Its outer shell is $3s^2 3p^1$, so it has 1 p electron. This fits perfectly because $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is amphoteric and reacts with both hot concentrated HCl and hot aqueous NaOH.
options.C: 2 p electrons would mean Si with $3s^2 3p^2$. But $\text{SiO}_2$ is acidic, it reacts with hot NaOH but does not react with HCl. So it cannot be the amphoteric oxide Y.
options.D: 3 p electrons would mean P with $3s^2 3p^3$. But phosphorus oxides like $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$ are strongly acidic, they react with base but not with acid. This is the opposite of amphoteric behaviour.
